dependencies.reason: authenticates API keys, PATs and the admin token, defines their stored records and hashing, and reports the caller to the scope check and the handlers
provides the user record, the user selector and the admin check that the admin key and token routes use
builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation

tasks.title: Fix the scope registry and install the PAT scope check
steps: Add the scope behaviours to internal/identity/scope_test.go (the registry table, the implication table, the refusal through the server pipeline, the pass for the admin token and API keys) and confirm they fail
Define the registry of exactly 32 scopes from the PRD's list, with a validator for one name and an accessor that returns all of them in the PRD's order

Implement the satisfaction rule: the needed scope itself; R:write for a needed R:read; keys:manage for keys:read; tokens:manage for tokens:write and tokens:read; tokens:write for tokens:read; nothing else, so changes:approve and checks:write are satisfied only by themselves and satisfy nothing else
Read the one scope a PAT needs from the scope declaration of package 02's route registration, which every route states when it is registered with internal/server; add no second way to declare it

Implement the scope check for step 6 of the check order: it reads the caller that authentication (package 04) reported; the admin token, an API key and a route without a declared scope pass; a PAT passes when its permissions satisfy the declared scope
On failure answer through package 02's error helper: HTTP 403, error_type insufficient_scope, a message naming the needed scope; no later check and no handler runs
Install the check in the scope position of package 02's pipeline through the composition of package 03, in internal/hub/identity.go

tasks.title: Validate, match and compare path globs
steps: Add the glob behaviours to internal/identity/pathglob_test.go (the validation table, the match table, the cover table and the soundness property) and confirm they fail

Implement validation of a decoded paths value: null or absent is unrestricted; refuse a value that is not an array, an empty array, more than 50 entries, an entry that is not a string, an empty glob, a glob longer than 255 characters, a glob starting with /; return an error that names the offending entry

Implement matching of one glob against one file path over the whole path, case-sensitively: ** is any run including /, * is any run without /, runs may be empty, every other character (including ?, [ and backslash) is literal; a run of three or more asterisks reads as ** followed by the rest
Implement matching against a token's list: a path is allowed when the list is absent or any glob matches

Implement the cover test: equal globs cover; otherwise the caller's glob is matched against the requested glob's text, where its * may take a run with no / and without the sequence **, and its ** any run
Implement the list form of the cover test that returns the first requested glob no caller glob covers
Write the soundness property over generated globs and paths: whenever the cover test accepts and the requested glob matches a path, the covering glob matches it too
Export the matcher under stable names and document that packages 18, 21, 22 and 29 call it to enforce paths on writes; the HTTP rows of the validation table are added by the token-creation task

tasks.title: Create personal access tokens
steps: Add the creation behaviours to internal/identity/token_routes_test.go against a hub started in-process with a temporary store and a test clock, and confirm they fail; add the HTTP rows of the paths validation table there too

Use the PAT table package 04 created and authenticates against (name, the ordered permissions list, the ordered paths list or null, the workspace slug or null, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at); add no table, no column and no schema step, and leave the hashing and the wire format to package 04

Define the Token JSON object with exactly the members token_id, user_id, name, permissions, paths, workspace, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at; null for unset members; timestamps through package 02's whole-second UTC format

Implement the minting operation as one exported function of internal/identity that takes the caller, the request (name, permissions, paths, expires), an optional workspace binding and, for hub-internal callers, an expiry instant in place of expires, can run inside the caller's transaction, and returns the stored token and its one-time value; it is the one way a PAT is created in production; besides POST /user/tokens its one caller is the minting component MintBound of package 08, and packages 15 and 45 mint only through MintBound

Validate in it: name 1 to 255 characters; permissions a non-empty array of registered scopes, duplicates dropped, order kept; expires an integer among 0, 30, 60, 90 with default 90; paths through the glob validation; every failure is 400 invalid_request and writes nothing

Write the token through the store-level PAT function of package 04, which this operation wraps: that function generates token_id (8) and secret (32) from [a-z0-9] with crypto/rand, generates the id again when it exists and stores only the hash; pass it expires_at as now plus expires times 24 hours, null for 0, or the caller's instant

Register POST /user/tokens as a creating route that declares scope tokens:manage and the show-once member token, so that a replay under the same Idempotency-Key answers 200 without the value (package 02's idempotency)
Answer 201 with the Token plus token; workspace is null on this route
Take the identity component's clock as a parameter so the tests can move time across expires_at
done_when: `go test ./internal/identity/... -count=1` passes with the token value absent from every stored column

tasks.title: Hold PAT callers to the subset rule
steps: Add the subset-rule tables to internal/identity/token_routes_test.go and confirm they fail

In the minting operation, after body validation and before the write, apply the rule only when the caller is a PAT: every requested permission must be in the caller's own list exactly, with no implication

For a caller PAT that has paths: refuse a request without paths (absent or null) with a message saying paths is required; otherwise require every requested glob to be covered by one of the caller's globs
On a violation answer 403 insufficient_scope with a message that contains the first offending permission in request order, or else the first offending glob; write nothing
Keep validation first: a body that is invalid and also violates the rule is answered 400
Leave API key callers unrestricted
Expose the rule as a function over (caller, requested permissions, requested paths) so the permission-change routes and packages 08 and 15 apply the same code

tasks.title: Read and revoke personal access tokens
steps: Add the read, revoke, ownership, scope and admin-token behaviours to internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, and the behaviours of the two hub-internal operations to internal/identity/token_ops_test.go, and confirm they fail

Register GET /user/tokens (scope tokens:read) as a list route with package 02's paging: every PAT of the caller's user in any state, bound ones included, ordered by created_at descending then token_id descending
Register GET /user/tokens/:token_id (scope tokens:read) answering the Token

Register DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id (scope tokens:manage): set revoked_at to now when it is null, including for an expired token and for the calling token itself; answer 200 with the Token; an already revoked token is answered 200 unchanged
Resolve :token_id through one lookup scoped to the caller's user, so that a missing id and another user's id give the same 404 not_found body; use it on every /user/tokens/:token_id route

Register every route under /user/keys and /user/tokens with package 04's needs-a-user mark (PLAT-FR-021), so that the admin token is answered 403 forbidden with package 04's message "this route needs a user"; write no second refusal in the handlers
Check that no Token object outside the creation response carries the token member or the secret text

Export from internal/identity/token.go the two operations hub-internal callers use inside a transaction of their own, with no route, no ownership check and no event: the revocation by id, RevokeTokenByID(tx, token_id), which sets revoked_at to now when it is null and leaves a revoked token unchanged, and the expiry update of one token by id, SetTokenExpiryByID(tx, token_id, instant), which sets expires_at in whole seconds and nothing else; an unknown token_id is the not-found error; neither commits; packages 45 and 47 call them for the hub credential of a sandbox

tasks.title: Change a token's permissions
steps: Add the permission-change behaviours to internal/identity/token_routes_test.go and confirm they fail
Register PUT, PATCH and DELETE on /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions, each declaring scope tokens:write and taking the body {permissions: string[]}
Order the handler's checks: ownership lookup (404), body validation (400), subset rule for a PAT caller (403), state (409 for a revoked or expired token), then the write
Validate: permissions must be an array of strings; PUT and PATCH refuse a string that is not a registered scope; PATCH and DELETE refuse an empty array; PUT accepts an empty array

PUT stores the list given with duplicates dropped; PATCH appends the scopes not yet present, in the order given; DELETE removes the given scopes and ignores strings the token does not have, registered or not
For a PAT caller apply the subset rule to the scopes the change would add (the scopes of the new list that the token does not have now); DELETE has no subset check
When the resulting list is empty, store the empty list and set revoked_at in the same transaction
Ignore body members named paths and workspace; never change paths, workspace, name or expires_at
Answer 200 with the Token after the change

tasks.title: List, refresh and revoke API keys
steps: Add the key behaviours to internal/identity/key_routes_test.go against a hub started in-process with a test clock and confirm they fail
Define the Key JSON object with exactly the members key_id, user_id, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at; never a secret
Register GET /user/keys (scope keys:read) as a list route: every key of the caller's user in any state, ordered by created_at descending then key_id descending
Register POST /user/keys/:key_id/refresh without a declared scope and not as a creating route; answer 403 forbidden when the caller is a PAT or the admin token, before the key is looked up
Resolve :key_id through one lookup scoped to the caller's user, so that a missing id and another user's id give the same 404 not_found

On refresh of a live key: generate a new 32-character secret from [0-9A-Za-z], store its hash in place of the old one, set expires_at to now plus the key's expires_days (null for 0), and answer 200 with key, key_id and expires_at; a revoked or expired key is 409 conflict and unchanged

Register DELETE /user/keys/:key_id (scope keys:manage): set revoked_at to now when it is null, including for an expired key and for the calling key itself; answer 200 with the Key; an already revoked key is answered 200 unchanged
Use package 04's key record, hashing and expiry predicate; add no second definition of them

tasks.title: Let an admin list and revoke any user's keys and tokens
steps: Add the admin route behaviours to internal/identity/admin_credential_routes_test.go and confirm they fail

Register GET /users/:id/keys, GET /users/:id/tokens, DELETE /users/:id/keys/:key_id and DELETE /users/:id/tokens/:token_id behind package 05's admin check, so that an API key of a role-user user and every PAT get 403 forbidden
Resolve :id with package 05's user selector (UUID, e-mail or username); an unknown user is 404 not_found
List with the same order and objects as the /user routes: newest first, any state, bound tokens included

Revoke by a lookup scoped to the selected user: a key or token that does not exist or belongs to another user is 404 not_found; set revoked_at when null (an expired one included); answer 200 with the object; an already revoked one is answered 200 unchanged

tasks.title: Add the parley keys and parley admin keys commands
steps: Add the command behaviours to internal/cli/keys_test.go and internal/cli/admin_keys_test.go against a stub hub and a temporary PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR, and confirm they fail

Add the command group keys with list, refresh and revoke, and the group admin keys with list <user> and revoke <user> <key_id>, under the root command, each declared through the command helper of package 09 with its method, path, arguments and auth value; a group without a subcommand prints help
keys list calls GET /user/keys and prints the body through package 09's output

Derive key_id from the configured credential for refresh and revoke: accept only the API key format parley_<8 characters>_<32 characters> from [0-9A-Za-z]; a PAT, the admin token or any other value is a client_error with exit 2 and no request

keys refresh: POST the refresh route, print the response, warn on stderr that the key is not shown again, then write api_key through the save function of package 09 in internal/cli/config.go (other keys kept, mode 0600); when the config file does not exist or cannot be written, write nothing, warn on stderr that the new key was not saved and exit 2 after the response has been printed

keys revoke: DELETE the key, print the response, clear api_key and user_id in the config file when it exists, and tell the user on stderr to run parley login; when the hub answers an error leave the file unchanged
admin keys list and revoke call GET /users/<user>/keys and DELETE /users/<user>/keys/<key_id> with each argument percent-encoded as one path segment; a wrong argument count is a usage_error

tasks.title: Add the parley tokens and parley admin tokens commands
steps: Add the command behaviours to internal/cli/tokens_test.go and internal/cli/admin_tokens_test.go against a stub hub and confirm they fail

Add the command group tokens with list, create, show, revoke, replace, add and remove, and the group admin tokens with list <user> and revoke <user> <token_id>, under the root command, each declared through the command helper of package 09

tokens create takes --name (required), --permissions (required, comma-separated), --paths (comma-separated, repeatable, values appended in order), --expires (integer, default 90); it posts name, permissions, expires and, only when --paths was given, paths to /user/tokens; it prints the response and warns on stderr that the value is not shown again
tokens list, show <token_id> and revoke <token_id> call GET /user/tokens, GET /user/tokens/<token_id> and DELETE /user/tokens/<token_id>

tokens replace, add and remove <token_id> --permissions <list> send PUT, PATCH and DELETE to /user/tokens/<token_id>/permissions with {permissions: [...]}; an empty --permissions value sends an empty array; replace and remove write a note on stderr when the returned Token has revoked_at set
A missing required flag, a wrong argument count or a non-integer --expires is a usage_error with exit 2 before any request; allowed lifetimes and scope names are left to the hub
admin tokens list and revoke call GET /users/<user>/tokens and DELETE /users/<user>/tokens/<token_id> with each argument percent-encoded as one path segment
Leave the --workspace flag of both tokens create and tokens list to package 08, which adds it to these two commands in internal/cli/tokens.go; without the flag tokens list calls GET /user/tokens only
